description:
Before adding one new holding to a portfolio: how much of it is already owned through the
        current funds, whether it adds an independent bet, what past crises would have done
        with it, and a decision sheet with three columns: now, the same money kept as cash,
        the money in the new holding. Typical questions: 'I'm thinking of adding $10,000 of
        QQQ with new cash: what changes versus keeping it in cash?'; 'Check before I buy
        SCHD.'; 'Test adding an ETF to my portfolio.'. Instead: for selling, reweighting or
        several changes at once, test_a_change. The 'after' portfolio was never held; it
        never says whether to buy. It does not recommend, predict or calculate tax.

amount.description: How much of it, in the same units as `holdings` (money when holdings are amounts).
amount.title: Amount

base.description: Currency code every figure is expressed in: USD, EUR, GBP, CAD… Default USD.
base.title: Base

holdings.description: What is held: {ticker: number}, 1 to 100 holdings. Weights in any scale (60/20/20 or 0.6/0.2/0.2) or money amounts in the base currency (60000/20000/20000): `units` says which; without it, holdings adding up to 1 or 100 are read as percentages, anything else as money, which makes the falls come out in money. Tickers as the exchange lists them (VOO, VWCE.DE, EQQQ.DE, XAW.TO; 'CASH.USD' for cash). Example: {"VTI": 60, "VXUS": 20, "BND": 20}.
holdings.title: Holdings

units.description: What the holdings' numbers are: 'money' (amounts in the base currency) or 'weights' (percentages or fractions). Omitted: holdings adding up to 1 or 100 are read as percentages, anything else as money, and the answer says so.
units.title: Units

name: check_before_you_buy

outputSchema.description: One addition measured on the portfolio it would join (counterfactual).

_fence.description: What these figures are and are not: descriptive, no forecast, no advice. Repeat its sense when presenting the result.

crises.description: Per past crisis: fall before and after, as fractions.

data.description: Where the prices came from and what was missing or repaired.

as_of.description: Last date of price history used.

missing.description: Tickers with no usable history (left out).

standins.description: Holdings measured through a stand-in with longer history: ticker, proxy, index, from, until, evidence.

overlap.description: How much of it is already owned: kind (fund, stock, opaque); for a fund already_share (share of its money in companies already held), seen_share, shared ([company, weight in it, weight in the portfolio]), source, as_of; for a stock already (share of the portfolio) and via.

top_risk.description: The holding carrying the most risk, and its share, before and after.

title: Check before you buy
